rubric_feedback: 1) q10f_surcharge requires 'the proclamation number or the document number' and refuses credit to an answer that identifies the instrument as '91 FR 9339, clause (1)'. That is a first-page FR citation to Proclamation 11012 and at least as traceable as the identifiers named; the rubric elsewhere (e.g. q2a_basis: 'FR Doc. 2026-17294 or 91 FR 54790') accepts the two interchangeably, so this criterion is inconsistent and arguably should accept a correct FR citation. 2) q14_3_jordan silently requires the list of six economies that imposed bans on top of the Jordan point; a submission that explains only Jordan's own basis (an accurate answer to the statement's main error) loses the point on an element it could not know was separately scored. Consider marking that clause 'welcome but not required'. 3) q1_dairy_xref and q4c_xref both test the same single sentence of Proclamation 11062(3), so one omission costs points twice on different questions. 4) Q15 concentrates 14 criteria on a single interpretive fork (whether the Canada IEEPA duties survived and how Executive Order 14289 orders the two duties); a submission that gets the ordering backwards loses almost the whole question, which is by design but makes Q15 a very low-information discriminator. 5) The Q11 do-not-count note on 'Proclamation 11056's suspension against its change of the effective date' sits close to a genuinely arguable discrepancy (the unconditional operative date against recitals attributing the lapse to Canada's August 21 conduct); a line explaining that the recitals describe rather than contradict the operative text would make the instruction clearer.
